standard.title: Concrete Pipes — Methods of Test (Second Revision) (कंक्रीट के पाइप — परीक्षण पद्धतियाँ (दूसरा पुनरीक्षण))
standard.description: This Indian Standard prescribes laboratory and on-site testing methods for carrying out physical, mechanical, hydraulic, and structural tests on precast concrete pipes—including reinforced concrete (RCC), unreinforced (PCC), and prestressed concrete (PSC) pipes—designed for both pressure and non-pressure applications to verify design properties.
standard.scope: This Indian Standard prescribes laboratory and on-site testing methods for carrying out physical, mechanical, hydraulic, and structural tests on precast concrete pipes—including reinforced concrete (RCC), unreinforced (PCC), and prestressed concrete (PSC) pipes—designed for both pressure and non-pressure applications to verify design properties.

certification.description: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 3597 is an analytical testing standard rather than a directly sold physical retail product, it does not carry an individual physical 'ISI Mark' on its own. However, compliance with its hydrostatic, crushing, water-absorption, and joints-tolerancing protocols is strictly required in laboratory accreditation audits (under NABL ISO/IEC 17025:2017) and public sector civil works audits (including PWDs, NHAI, state water boards, and the CPWD).
requirements: Hydrostatic barrel pressure must be maintained by continuous water pumping using a throttling device for 1 minute and 30 seconds for each 10 mm of wall thickness.

For precast concrete pipes (IS 458), the wall thickness used to compute pressure duration shall be the full barrel wall thickness. For prestressed concrete pipes (IS 784), it shall be the core concrete thickness.

If the application of water pressure results in the formation of beads of water or droplets on the pipe's exterior surface, the pressure-holding period must be extended to twice the standard duration.

The boiling water absorption is calculated by drying the full-wall specimen to constant mass at 105°C to 115°C (M1), boiling continuously for 5 hours, cooling naturally in water for 14 to 24 hours, and weighing the surface-dried specimen immediately (M2) to calculate weight gain percentage.
Water absorption percentage is calculated using the equation: [(M2 - M1) / M1] * 100, representing the concrete specimen's permeability.
The socket diameter is verified using a specialized gauge to check the out-of-roundness sway (S) by touching two circumferential points B and B1 relative to bottom anchor A.
The socket diameter sway is checked using the formula: S = 2 * [h * (D1 - h)]^(1/2), where D1 is the maximum permissible socket diameter.

For roll-on and confined joints, the ring gauge's inside diameter must be larger than the maximum spigot diameter by exactly 1 mm to allow clearance. The spacing between gauge points is computed as: Spigot Outside Diameter + 1 mm + 1 mm.

Protective cement mortar coatings on finished pipes are evaluated using a specialized permeability cup and acrylic water tube clamped over the coating with 10 mm wire rope and eye-bolts under compressed air.

Before testing, the pipe's mortar cover coat must be fully saturated, the dry surface scraped with a wire brush, the equipment clamped, water filled into the acrylic tube, and pneumatic pressure applied.

Crushing strength (cracking and ultimate load) is evaluated by applying continuous vertical parallel line loads through a top wooden block and supporting the barrel on two parallel bottom wooden strips, all padded with resilient rubber strips.

All observed or calculated physical parameters, test loads, and joint clearances must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
